easy.def: A message sent by computer.
examples: I got an email.
She sent an email.
The email came this morning.

more.def: A message that is typed and sent over the internet from one computer to another.
examples: I sent an email to my teacher.
She read the email from her aunt.
The email had a photo of the puppy.

easy.def: To come out from a source.
examples: Light emanates from the sun.
A smell emanated from the kitchen.
Heat emanates from the fire.

more.def: To flow or come out from a source.
examples: A sweet smell emanated from the bakery.
Light emanated from the lamp.
Warmth emanated from the stove.

easy.def: A raised bank of earth beside a road, track or river.
examples: The train ran along the embankment.
We sat on the embankment.
The embankment is high.

more.def: A raised bank of earth or stone built to hold back water or to carry a road or railway.
examples: The train ran along the top of the embankment.
Grass grew on the steep embankment beside the river.
Workers built an embankment to stop the river from flooding.

easy.def: To start a trip, or to go onto a ship or plane.
examples: We embark at noon.
They embarked on a trip.
The sailors embarked.

more.def: To get on a ship or a plane to start a trip, or to begin something new.
examples: The passengers embarked on the ship at noon.
The explorers embarked on a long trip across the desert.
She embarked on a new hobby: learning to paint.

easy.def: To make someone feel shy or silly.
examples: It would embarrass me to sing alone.
Please do not embarrass me in front of my friends.
My loud hiccups embarrassed me.

more.def: To make someone feel awkward or ashamed in front of others.
examples: Tripping on stage embarrassed him, but he kept going.
He did not mean to embarrass his sister by telling the story.
Forgetting her lines embarrassed the young actor.

easy.def: Feeling shy or silly because of something that happened.
examples: I was embarrassed when I tripped.
She felt embarrassed.
He turned red and was embarrassed.

more.def: Feeling awkward or ashamed in front of other people.
examples: He was embarrassed when he forgot his lines.
She felt embarrassed when she called the teacher "Mom."
The embarrassed boy hid his face.

easy.def: Making you feel shy or silly in front of others.
examples: It was embarrassing to trip.
That is an embarrassing mistake.
The song was embarrassing.

more.def: Causing you to feel awkward, shy or ashamed in front of other people.
examples: It was embarrassing when I called my teacher "Mom."
He found it embarrassing to sing alone.
Tripping in front of the whole class was embarrassing.

easy.def: Feeling shy or silly in front of others.
examples: He felt embarrassment.
Her face showed embarrassment.
The embarrassment passed.

more.def: A feeling of being awkward or ashamed in front of other people.
examples: He turned red with embarrassment.
Her embarrassment grew when everyone laughed.
The embarrassment faded after a while.

easy.def: A building where officials from another country work.
examples: The embassy has a flag.
We went to the embassy.
The embassy is in the capital.

more.def: A building in a foreign country where officials from another country work.
examples: The French embassy flies the flag of France.
We went to the embassy to get a visa.
The embassy is in the capital city.

easy.def: To push something firmly into something else.
examples: The nail embedded in the wood.
The stone was embedded in the dirt.
A shell is embedded in the sand.

more.def: To fix something firmly into a surface.
examples: The stone was embedded in the wall.
A nail embedded itself in the tire.
Tiny shells are embedded in the cliff.

easy.def: A glowing piece of wood after a fire.
examples: The ember glowed.
An ember is hot.
The fire left embers.

more.def: A glowing piece of coal or wood left after a fire has died down.
examples: An ember glowed in the fireplace.
The embers were still warm in the morning.
Sparks flew from the glowing ember.

easy.def: A picture or sign that stands for something.
examples: The bird is the emblem.
The flag is an emblem.
A badge has an emblem.

more.def: A picture, design or object that stands for a group or an idea.
examples: An eagle is the emblem of the country.
The team's emblem is on its shirts.
A heart is an emblem of love.

easy.def: To be a perfect example of something.
examples: She embodies kindness.
He embodies courage.
The statue embodies hope.

more.def: To be a perfect example or sign of an idea or quality.
examples: She embodies kindness in everything she does.
The statue embodies hope for the town.
The hero embodies courage in the story.

easy.def: To hug.
examples: The mother embraced her child.
They embraced.
I embraced my friend.

more.def: To hold someone in your arms to show love.
examples: She embraced her friend at the station.
The two brothers embraced after the long trip.
Grandma embraced me tightly.

easy.def: To sew pictures on cloth.
examples: Grandma embroiders flowers.
She embroidered a heart on the pillow.
He embroidered his name.

more.def: To decorate cloth by sewing a design onto it with thread.
examples: Grandma embroidered flowers on the pillow.
She embroidered a heart on my jacket.
He embroidered his name on the towel.

easy.def: Pretty sewn pictures on cloth.
examples: The pillow has embroidery.
Grandma does embroidery.
The embroidery is pink.

more.def: Decorations sewn onto cloth with thread.
examples: The pillow had embroidery of flowers.
Grandma does embroidery in the evenings.
The embroidery on the shirt was done by hand.

easy.def: A green jewel.
examples: The ring has an emerald.
An emerald is green.
The emerald sparkles.

more.def: A bright green gem that is valuable and used in jewelry.
examples: The ring has a sparkling emerald.
The emerald was a deep, bright green.
The queen wore an emerald necklace.

easy.def: To come out of something.
examples: The puppy emerged from the box.
A bear emerged from the cave.
The sun emerged.

more.def: To come out from a hidden or covered place.
examples: The butterfly emerged from its cocoon.
A bear emerged from its cave in the spring.
The sun emerged from behind the clouds.

easy.def: A sudden, scary event when you need help fast.
examples: This door is only for an emergency.
The nurse handled the emergency.
There was an emergency.

more.def: A sudden and serious event that needs quick action.
examples: Call for help in an emergency.
The hospital treats emergencies all night.
In an emergency, stay calm.

easy.def: To leave your country to live in another.
examples: They emigrated to Canada.
My family emigrated.
He plans to emigrate.

more.def: To leave your own country in order to live in another country.
examples: Her family emigrated to Canada when she was five.
Many people emigrated to find work.
He plans to emigrate to Australia.

easy.def: A person who is sent with a message.
examples: The emissary brought a letter.
The king sent an emissary.
The emissary rode far.

more.def: A person sent to carry a message or do a job for a leader or country.
examples: The king sent an emissary to the neighboring land.
The emissary carried a message of peace.
An emissary traveled far to bring the news.

easy.def: To give off.
examples: The lamp will emit light.
The fire emits heat.
The stove emitted a smell.

more.def: To send out something such as light, heat, sound or a smell.
examples: The lamp emits a soft glow.
The campfire emitted heat and a little smoke.
The old radio emitted a buzzing sound.

easy.def: A strong feeling, like joy or fear.
examples: Joy is an emotion.
She showed her emotion.
Anger is an emotion.

more.def: A feeling, such as happiness, sadness, anger or fear.
examples: Joy and sadness are emotions.
He spoke with strong emotion when he said goodbye.
Actors show emotion with their faces.

easy.def: Having strong feelings.
examples: He was emotional at the end.
The movie was emotional.
She felt emotional.

more.def: Having to do with feelings, or showing strong feelings.
examples: The goodbye was emotional for everyone.
She felt emotional and cried happy tears.
The movie had an emotional ending.

easy.def: The ruler of a large empire.
examples: The emperor lived in a palace.
The emperor was powerful.
The emperor wore a robe.

more.def: The male ruler of a very large land, called an empire.
examples: The emperor lived in a grand palace.
In ancient Rome, the emperor had great power.
The people bowed to the emperor.

easy.def: Special attention put on something important.
examples: The teacher put emphasis on the word.
He put emphasis on being kind.
There is an emphasis on reading.

more.def: Special importance or attention given to something, or extra force when saying a word.
examples: The teacher put emphasis on the first step.
He said "never" with emphasis.
Our school places an emphasis on reading.

easy.def: To show that something is very important.
examples: The teacher emphasized the rule.
I emphasize this point.
She emphasized the word.

more.def: To give special attention to something to show that it is important.
examples: The teacher emphasized the importance of reading every night.
She said the word loudly to emphasize it.
The coach emphasized teamwork before the big game.

easy.def: In a strong way that leaves no doubt.
examples: He said no emphatically.
She emphatically nodded.
They emphatically cheered.

more.def: In a strong and clear way that shows you mean it.
examples: "No!" she said emphatically.
He emphatically shook his head.
The coach emphatically told the team to stay calm.

easy.def: A large group of lands ruled by one leader.
examples: The Roman Empire was huge.
The empire had many lands.
The emperor ruled the empire.

more.def: A group of countries or lands under the control of one ruler or government.
examples: The Roman Empire once covered much of Europe.
The emperor ruled a vast empire.
The empire grew as it took over new lands.

easy.def: To pay someone to work for you.
examples: The shop employs ten people.
The farm employed workers.
He employed a helper.

more.def: To give someone a job and pay them.
examples: The bakery employs ten people.
The farm employed extra workers at harvest.
The school employs many teachers.

easy.def: A person who works for someone for pay.
examples: The employee helped us find the book.
An employee at the store wore a badge.
He is an employee at the bank.

more.def: A person who is paid to work for a business or a person.
examples: An employee at the shop helped us find the right size.
The company has fifty employees.
The new employee started work on Monday.

easy.def: A person or company that pays workers.
examples: My employer is kind.
Her employer is the school.
The employer pays me.

more.def: A person or company that gives people jobs and pays them.
examples: My mom's employer is a big company.
The employer thanked the workers.
The school is the largest employer in town.

easy.def: Having a job.
examples: He is looking for employment.
Employment is important.
She found employment.

more.def: The state of having paid work.
examples: Employment in the area has grown.
She found employment at the library.
The new factory gave employment to many people.

easy.def: A big shop that sells many kinds of things.
examples: We went to the emporium.
The emporium sells toys.
The emporium is big.

more.def: A large store that sells many different kinds of goods.
examples: The old emporium sold everything from toys to tools.
We found a gift at the emporium in town.
The toy emporium has shelves that go up to the ceiling.

easy.def: A woman who rules an empire.
examples: The empress lived in a palace.
The empress waved to the people.
A queen or an empress.

more.def: A woman who rules an empire, or the wife of an emperor.
examples: The empress ruled a huge land from her golden palace.
The people bowed when the empress walked by.
In the story, the empress wore a crown covered in jewels.

easy.def: The feeling of there being nothing there.
examples: We felt the emptiness.
The emptiness of the room.
The emptiness made us sad.

more.def: The state of having nothing inside, or a lonely feeling that something is missing.
examples: The emptiness of the big room echoed with our footsteps.
She felt an emptiness after her friend moved away.
The emptiness of the desert stretched in every direction.

easy.def: With nothing inside.
examples: The box is empty.
My cup is empty.
The room was empty.

more.def: Having nothing inside.
examples: The box was empty when we opened it.
She found an empty seat on the bus.
The empty classroom was quiet.

easy.def: To take everything out.
examples: Empty the bucket.
She emptied the bag.
He empties the trash.

more.def: To take everything out of something.
examples: Empty your pockets before you wash your pants.
She emptied the bucket of sand.
Dad empties the trash every Tuesday.

easy.def: A big bird from Australia that cannot fly.
examples: An emu ran.
The emu is tall.
The emu cannot fly.

more.def: A tall, flightless bird of Australia with long legs and shaggy feathers.
examples: An emu ran across the field.
The emu is the second tallest bird in the world.
Emus can run very fast.
